subject: SIG evidence provenance, redaction and delivery plan
messages:
From: Audrey Chen <audrey.chen@horizonbank.com>
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: LegalOps <legal@horizonbank.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial evidence request + redaction constraints for SIG RFI

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we move toward formal SIG submission for Horizon Bank, Legal has asked for a clear mapping of control provenance and a defensible redaction policy for any customer-impacting telemetry. Specifically we need:

- An itemized control crosswalk mapping SIG questions to Redwood controls and artifacts.
- A list of sample artifacts (logs, config exports, design docs) and any PHI/PII fields that should be redacted before delivery.
- A proposed delivery cadence and secure link for artifact pickup.

Can you provide a plan and sample packet (redaction checklist + manifest) by COB Monday? We can extend the review window if you need it, just confirm a target.

Audrey
Audrey Chen
Senior InfoSec Manager, Horizon Bank

--
Attachment: request_form.pdf (application/pdf stub)

From: sean.gallagher@redwood.com
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: audrey.chen@horizonbank.com, legal@horizonbank.com
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial evidence request + redaction constraints for SIG RFI

Audrey — thanks for the clarity. Kimberly / Marissa, looping you both in to own evidence extraction and redaction. High level plan I propose:

1) Control crosswalk (deliverable: control_crosswalk_v2.xlsx) — maps each SIG control to our control name, control owner, evidence location, and a sample artifact. Kimber can confirm owners.
2) Redaction guidance (deliverable: redaction_guidelines_v1.pdf) — checklist by artifact type (logs, screenshots, csv exports) with fields recommended for redaction and the rationale.
3) Manifest + secure delivery (deliverable: evidence_manifest.csv + one-time shared link) — list of files to be delivered, SHA256, and minimal metadata. We will host on a short-lived signed URL and provide instructions for access auditing.

Timeline: ship draft crosswalk + redaction checklist by Mon 06/08 EOD PT; finalize artifacts and share secure link Wed 06/10. If Legal needs earlier, we can push the draft to Mon morning but will need extra hands for the redaction scrub.

Kimberly — can you confirm control owners and whether we can generate log extracts with field-level redaction on the timeline above? Marissa — can you coordinate packaging and the secure share?

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Security & Compliance Partnerships
Redwood Inference

--
(Inline: brief quoted request from Audrey)

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, audrey.chen@horizonbank.com
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 12:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial evidence request + redaction constraints for SIG RFI

Thanks Sean — I can own the control crosswalk and the redaction rules. Quick notes from infra side: 

- Control provenance: our config management and deployment tags provide an audit trail for control changes (CMDB export + deployment hashes). We can map SIG control IDs to our control IDs and attach config snapshots.
- Logs: we will produce exported logs with PII columns removed via our log exporter. For fields that are semi-structured (json payloads), we will provide a sanitized sample and the full schema so Horizon can validate redactions.
- KMS/custody artifacts: we will provide architecture diagrams and key-rotation statements; we cannot share private key material — we'll include attestations.

I attached a redaction checklist draft and a first-pass crosswalk (skeleton). I flagged a few items that need product team confirmation (rows with NOTE: product-confirm).

Deliverables attached: control_crosswalk_v2.xlsx (skeleton), redaction_guidelines_v1.pdf (draft), evidence_manifest.csv (empty template).

Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: control_crosswalk_v2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet stub), redaction_guidelines_v1.pdf (application/pdf stub), evidence_manifest.csv (text/csv stub)

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: audrey.chen@horizonbank.com, legal@horizonbank.com
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG evidence provenance, redaction and delivery plan

Team — quick status update and a couple of asks from packaging side:

- I pulled the flagged 'product-confirm' rows and confirmed owners for 12 items with Product. Two items will require a short artifact extract from runtime telemetry (expected size ~45MB).
- Redaction approach: we'll run a two-pass scrub — automated field-level redaction followed by a manual spot check on samples. For the telemetry extracts we will provide both a redacted sample and a schema-only file (no payloads).
- Delivery: planning to stage artifacts to a signed S3 location with 7-day expiry. Access will be logged; we'll provide a link and one-time access code.

Asking Legal: do you need a separate notarized attestation for KMS/key custody statements or will a signed statement from our CISO suffice?

Target: final upload Wed 06/10 10:00 PT, handoff meeting Wed 06/10 11:00 PT (30 min).

Marissa Cole
Principal Compliance Engineer
Redwood Inference

--
(Inline: excerpt from control_crosswalk_v2.xlsx showing 5 sample rows)

From: LegalOps <legal@horizonbank.com>
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: audrey.chen@horizonbank.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG evidence provenance, redaction and delivery plan

Sean / team — thanks for the plan and the draft materials. A few Legal clarifications: 

1) Notarized attestation is preferred for key custody language in our formal submission packet, but depending on timing we will accept a CISO-signed declaration for the initial intake if accompanied by the architecture diagrams and rotation logs.
2) For any telemetry extracts: we require a redaction manifest indicating which columns were removed and the rationale. That can be a separate CSV.
3) Please maintain a tamper-evident trail. SHA256 hashes plus the manifest are sufficient for us.

If you can incorporate the notarization step into the final timeline (or confirm the CISO-signed interim submission), we'll review the packet and confirm acceptance.

—Legal Ops
Horizon Bank

--
(Attachment: legal_requirements_0609.pdf stub)

From: sean.gallagher@redwood.com
To: audrey.chen@horizonbank.com, legal@horizonbank.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2026 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: SIG packet delivery plan + next steps

Audrey / Legal — finalizing schedule and confirming handoff details per your asks. Deliverables and timeline below: 

- Mon 06/08 (draft delivered): control_crosswalk_v2.xlsx, redaction_guidelines_v1.pdf, evidence_manifest.csv (manifest template).
- Wed 06/10 10:00 PT (final upload): staged artifacts at signed link (7-day expiry), evidence_manifest.csv populated with filename, SHA256, size, and redaction flags.
- Wed 06/10 11:00 PT (handoff): 30-minute call to walk the manifest and confirm acceptance.
- Notarization: Redwood CISO can sign an interim declaration for initial intake; we will provide notarized key custodial attestation within three business days of acceptance.

Access and tamper evidence: each file will be accompanied by SHA256 and logged access. Telemetry extracts will include a redaction_manifest_telemetry.csv listing removed columns and justification.

If that works, I'll schedule the handoff meeting and produce the signed interim CISO declaration.

Thanks everyone — appreciate the fast turnaround.

Sean Gallagher
Director, Security & Compliance Partnerships
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: control_crosswalk_v2.xlsx, redaction_guidelines_v1.pdf, evidence_manifest.csv (finalized); Delivery link (https://redwood-secure.example.com/s/hzn-5421-evidence)
